sources.entry: Downie - Video downloader for macOS with support for YouTube and other 1200 sites.

summary.name: Downie
summary.one_liner: Downie is a paid video downloader for macOS that saves videos from YouTube, Vimeo and over a thousand other sites.
use_cases: download YouTube videos on a Mac
extract audio tracks as podcasts or music
convert videos to MP4 for iPhone or iPad
summary.what_it_does: Downie is a native macOS app that downloads videos from YouTube, Vimeo, Youku, Dailymotion and over 1,000 other sites, with a single click or pasted link. It can fetch the highest available quality, including 4K for YouTube. Postprocessing can convert downloads to MP4 for iPhone or iPad or extract only the audio track. Download history syncs over iCloud across the user's Macs to avoid duplicates. For unsupported sites, a built-in browser can detect and grab the video, and browser extensions for Safari, Chrome and Firefox send links to the app.
notable: Supports over 1,000 sites with user-guided extraction for unsupported ones
Fetches 4K YouTube video and can convert to MP4 or audio-only
iCloud history sync across Macs to prevent duplicate downloads
Not on the Mac App Store; sold directly or via Setapp and an EU third-party marketplace
caveats: Paid: one-time license listed at $19.99 USD (base price EUR), with Setapp subscription at $14.99/mo as an alternative
Not distributed through Apple's App Store because of YouTube download rules; EU buyers use a third-party marketplace
Licenses issued after March 2025 do not work on macOS 10.15 or lower; older builds are linked for older macOS versions
